findings.title: Migration crashes when no persisted embed_category setting exists
findings.body: The migration unconditionally indexes `[0]['id']` from the `embed_category` query. Site settings that retain their default are commonly not persisted in `site_settings`, and new installs also have no legacy `embed_category` row, so this query can return no rows and raise before the fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` is reached. This prevents the database migration from completing. Handle an empty result before reading the ID and then use the uncategorized fallback.

findings.title: Legacy URL-form hosts are copied without normalization and stop matching
findings.body: The migration inserts each legacy host string directly, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s normalization callback. The previous setting accepted values such as `http://discourse.org` and URLs with paths, but `record_for_host` later compares the stored `host` column directly against `URI(referer).host` (for example, `discourse.org`). Consequently every migrated host configured with a scheme or path will no longer be allowed, disabling embeds and retrieval for those existing installations. Normalize each migrated host before insertion (and use bound inserts rather than SQL interpolation).

findings.title: Allowed hosts containing an allowed port can never match
findings.body: Validation explicitly accepts hosts with ports (for example `example.com:8443`), and the normalization callback preserves that port. However, `URI(host).host` returns only `example.com`, while this query compares it to the stored `example.com:8443`, so `host_allowed?` always returns false for such a record. Either reject ports if they are unsupported or normalize/query the stored value consistently with URI parsing.

findings.title: Duplicate hosts can route embeds to an arbitrary category
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation or database unique index for `host`, while `record_for_host` resolves a host using `where(...).first` without ordering. Staff can create the same host more than once with different category assignments, after which imported embeds are assigned according to whichever duplicate the database happens to return. Enforce case-insensitive uniqueness (ideally with a matching database index) so each host has one deterministic category relationship.

findings.title: Blank host submissions raise instead of returning a validation error
findings.body: The `before_validation` callback calls `sub!` on `self.host` unconditionally. A create or update request missing `embeddable_host[host]` therefore raises `NoMethodError` before `validates_format_of` can report an invalid record, producing a 500 response from the admin endpoint. Guard the normalization callback for a nil host so malformed requests receive the normal validation error.
